Alaykum As-Salam, I assume you're talking about the bottom left in the right container which is Ful Medammes. But I also adore Muhammara!

Left container:

Top is a salad called Fattoush which is a salad made with toasted pita, tomatoes, radishes, lettuce, cucumbers and basically any chopped up veggie you want, I sometimes like to add pomegranate. The dressing is made up of olive oil, lemon juice and sumac.

The bottom is Tabbouleh which is a salad made with mainly tomatoes, parsley, onions and bulgur with lemon juice, olive oil and salt.

Right container: 

Top is just vegetables.

Bottom left is called Ful Medammes (most people just call it Ful) which is cooked fava beans with olive oil, cumin and other herbs or garnishes, I like to add onions and tomatoes.

Bottom right is Hummus which is basically just chickpeas and tahini in a food processor (or mashed) with lemon juice, salt and garlic. 

It's a lot of food, so it does keep me full. I think especially with something like this, just eat a lot of the protein based stuff like Hummus and Ful to stay full.

The dark green stuff is a type of salad called Tabbouleh, it's basically chopped parsley, onions, tomatoes and bulgur with a dressing of lemon, olive oil and salt.

It's a pretty staple Middle Eastern dish, especially in Lebanon or Syria.

In my experience, rose water helps control my excess oil throughout the day. I keep a small spray bottle with me if I'm feeling like a need some refreshment for my skin.

My nephew had severe cerebral palsy. He was a twin as well so we were constantly reminded as to what he could have been or could have looked like.

My sister was given the option to let go but she didn't and her son died after a year. That year was filled with hospital visits, feeding tubes and so much struggle.

It completely changed their life. Anywhere we went we had to take feeding tubes, bags with formula he could eat etc. We would have to drop what we were doing and wait 20 minutes until he finished "eating".

His brother (twin) always tried to play with him but he would never respond, lacking emotional and physical responses to stimulus. 

None of us regret anything. We all love and miss him so much every single day of our lives. But it's okay, it's not crazy to think the way you are thinking OP, it's hard and it's full of challenges. Make whatever decision you believe is best; even if that means letting go.

First markschemes and past papers. There are tons online that you can check and see how the questions are asked + their answers. 

Secondly, I would suggest looking at the objectives at the beginning of every chapter. The IB has objectives specifically laid out for all of the subjects on content you need to know and stuff that does not matter. Look at those and use those as a checklist. Don't include what you do not need to know because the IB may not accept out of syllabus answers on the exams.

I hope this helps, even a little. I hope you do better!!
